main_text.p: 1. Vocali brevi.ut: θεὸς, γυνή. [Quandoque tamen breves ejusmodi syllabę fiunt ancipites: de quâ re postea.]
2. Apostropho; qui vocales breves duntaxat resecat.
3. Accentu. Sic α, ι, υ, finalia, accentu inscripto destituta, brevia intelliguntur.

III. [Excipe: 1. α productum, in Nominibus desinentibus in ᾰ, ῃ, ῳ, ία, substantivis & adjectivis fœmininis, αια polysyllabis, εια derivatis verbalibus, fœmininis denique dualis numeri. ut: λήδα, Κιϑαρῳδα, πηγή, φιλοσοφία, ἡ ἀγία, σεληνοαία, περισσεία, τὰ μύρα. Præter duo ista; ἡ ἁλία, ἡ πέτρα.]
2. ι finale productum, in quod contractio facta est. ut: ὀφίι, ὀφι.
3. υ finale productum, in tertiis personis Verborum in μι. ut: ἐδύ, ἐφυ.)
II. Longa syllaba cognoscitur quatuor modis.
II. Anceps (sive communis) syllaba, usu potis-

page.notes: Greek text is printed in a small, worn typeface; the Greek transcription is approximate and marked as such only where I was unsure. The catchword "potis-" is at the foot of the page as a broken word. Marginal signs III., II., II. are side-note signature-like markers, shown as notes.
